stories.title: Germany set to blame Russia for airport explosive-laden drone incident
stories.summary: Berlin is set to formally blame Russia for an incident involving drones at a strategic airport on the night of August 4-5, including one that was found carrying explosives. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt are expected to accuse a Russian intelligence service of being behind the incident. It would be the first time Germany formally blames Moscow for an incident like this one.

stories.title: Pistol in a lake gives hope for French cold case
stories.summary: Police investigating the unsolved murder of a British family in France 14 years ago have an unexpected new clue with the discovery of a Luger pistol in the waters of a nearby lake. One of the few certainties in the killings of Saad al-Hilli with his wife and mother-in-law – as well as a passing cyclist – is that they were shot through the head with a Luger model P06, a type used by the Swiss army until around 1960. Now France's cold case unit has confirmed the discovery of a Luger in Lake Annecy, not far from the scene of the murders in September 2012. According to Marianne magazine, which broke the story, it was British tourists on 20 August who found the weapon lying in two metres of water. At first they thought it was a water pistol, but realised their mistake when they felt its weight. The discovery was made near the very camping site – Le Solitaire du Lac – where the al-Hillis were staying in their caravan, Marianne reported. Forensic experts are now examining the weapon, which has been badly damaged by its time under water, to see if it is indeed a P06 model. It is estimated that around 60,000 Luger P06s were manufactured. But the number of Luger pistols in general that were made is more like three million. Exhaustive investigations in France and the UK have left police no closer to understanding who carried out the al-Hilli murders and why. Over the years a series of leads have been pursued then dropped. A British national of Iraqi birth, Saad al-Hilli was holidaying with his family in the picturesque countryside of Lake Annecy in eastern France.

stories.title: Rosatom says practical international economic cooperation necessary in Arctic
stories.summary: Alexey Likhachev emphasized that the region required a working mechanism, not a club for declarations
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 1.

Prioritizing the establishment of a multilateral platform focused on practical economic and infrastructure cooperation in the Arctic covering freight transport, ports, energy, joint projects, and the safety and sustainability of navigation is logical, Chief Executive Officer of the Rosatom state corporation.
Alexey Likhachev said.
"Absolutely yes (regarding the need of an international cooperation format - TASS).
The entire world is currently in the process of shaping a new political system.
This process is not yet complete.
On the one hand, it is evident that Russia will play an important and worthy role in it.

On the other hand, we do not seek hegemony and, respecting our national interests, stand ready, as the President says, for mutually beneficial cooperation with all who are prepared for it," he said in an interview with the Expert magazine.

The emergence of a multilateral platform in the Arctic, focused primarily on practical economic and infrastructure cooperation, such as cargo transport, ports, energy, joint projects, and the safety and sustainability of navigation, seems logical to me.
We need a working mechanism, not a club for declarations," the chief executive added.
